children: The orders include projects from NTPC Renewable Energy, Jindal India Power, Purvah Green Power and other major producers

Adani Wind, the wind energy business of Adani New Industries, has secured 696.2 MW of orders from five power producers as it expands its customer base beyond the Adani Group amid growing demand for higher-capacity wind turbines.

The orders include 300 MW from Purvah Green Power, 155 MW from Jindal India Power, 109.2 MW from NTPC Renewable Energy, 82.5 MW from Aditya Birla Renewables and 49.5 MW from Integrum Energy. The projects will use 5.2 MW, 5 MW and 3.3 MW turbine platforms across Karnataka, Gujarat and Maharashtra, according to sources cited in a media report.

Purvah Green Power, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, has placed the largest order at 300 MW. The contract covers 60 turbines of Adani Wind's 5 MW platform for deployment in Bellary, Karnataka. Jindal India Power, part of the BC Jindal Group, has ordered 155 MW through 31 turbines of the same 5 MW platform. The machines are planned for installation in Davanagere, Karnataka.

NTPC Renewable Energy has ordered 21 turbines rated at 5.2 MW each for its Khavda project in Gujarat. Aditya Birla Renewables and Integrum Energy will use Adani Wind's 3.3 MW platform for projects in Bhuj, Gujarat, and Nandurbar, Maharashtra, respectively.

The latest orders have taken Adani Wind's cumulative order book from independent power producers outside the Adani Group beyond 1 GW. The company is seeking to strengthen its third-party business as India's wind market expands and turbine manufacturers compete for new projects.

As per the report, Adani Wind is also planning to raise annual manufacturing capacity at its Mundra facility in Gujarat from 2.25 GW to 5 GW. The company has set a longer-term target of reaching 10 GW of annual capacity, which could support both domestic demand and overseas opportunities.

The company's 5 MW MWL-185 turbine has a rotor diameter of 185 metres and a hub height of 140 metres and is designed for low- to moderate-wind conditions. Its 5.2 MW MWL-160 is among the higher-capacity onshore turbine models included in the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's Approved List of Models and Manufacturers.
India had 59.2 GW of installed wind power capacity, with another 43 GW under implementation, taking the combined operational and under-development capacity beyond 100 GW.

Domestic wind turbine manufacturing capacity has more than doubled from around 12 GW in fiscal 2023 to over 24 GW annually. The industry is targeting installations of around 8 GW in fiscal 2027, while annual additions are projected to reach 13.2 GW by fiscal 2031.

India added a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in fiscal 2026, as developers increasingly moved towards larger turbines and wider rotor diameters. Higher-capacity machines can improve generation and optimise land use, although project economics depend on wind conditions, site constraints and infrastructure availability.
